title: The Broken Thorn
premise: Ulyana Quintana, an exiled storm-caller, has spent his life hidden in the Thorn Valley, the one place magic cannot follow him. When a prophecy book written a century ago names tonight's date as the night his soul is claimed, he learns he was sold to the court beneath the mountain before his birth—and that staying invisible was never an option. With thirteen turns of the moon remaining, Ulyana must leave the valley with a disgraced archivist and a thief who owes him her life, crossing lands where his storm-magic marks him as prey. At the mountain court he discovers the soul that was sold was never fully his: half of it belongs to the valley itself, and reclaiming it will unmake the sanctuary that sheltered every exile within. In the end, Ulyana chooses truth over belonging—returning his stolen half, shattering the prophecy, and freeing both himself and the valley at the cost of the only home he has ever known.
about_author: Xanthe Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped cave systems beneath real mountains and never stopped wondering what lived in the unmapped dark. They write fantasy about people whose homes are also their prisons.

chapters.title: The Date That Already Happened
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Working in the valley's archive, Ulyana finds a century-old prophecy book naming tonight's date beside his own name. The ink is fresh. He tells no one, but the valley's wards flicker for the first time in living memory. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Ulyana tests his storm-calling at the wardline and feels something on the other side answer—a cold, patient attention. Elder Maren catches him and reveals she has read the same page. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; he must leave by morning.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Disgraced archivist Sef Idris offers to guide him; a decade ago Ulyana's silence saved Sef from exile for falsifying records. Sef knows where the prophecy book came from: the court beneath Mount Vhalen. Beat: uneasy alliance built on old debts.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Maren gives Ulyana a moon-calendar charm and a warning: if the thirteenth turn wanes with his soul still claimed, the court takes everything he loves too. He crosses the wardline and his magic roars back like a freed animal. Beat: exhilaration laced with terror.

chapters.title: Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Sef narrates their first days on the road, watching Ulyana struggle to control power he buried for twenty years. A storm they cause drowns a village's fields instead of saving them. Beat: guilt—the price of survival begins showing its face.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Owed Him
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. In the city of Corvane they find Ryn Osk, a thief Ulyana once shielded from a mob, now working for information brokers. She agrees to help reach the mountain—for a price: the name of whoever sold him. Beat: loyalty tested against curiosity.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Sold
chapters.summary: POV Ryn. Breaking into a broker's vault, Ryn finds a sales ledger: Ulyana's soul was purchased by Lady Vessarine of the under-court, paid for with a favor granted to someone in Thorn Valley. Beat: betrayal's first shadow—who at home signed?

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Moon
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. The court sends hollow-eyed hunters who feed on named souls. Ambushed at a river crossing, Ulyana kills for the first time and discovers his storms hurt worse when he's afraid. Beat: survival costs innocence; Sef is wounded.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Sef. While Ulyana sleeps, Sef confesses to Ryn that he helped catalog the original sale a century ago as an apprentice—he knew more than he admitted. Ryn keeps his secret, barely. Beat: loyalty vs. truth tightens around Sef's throat.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers Him
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Refugees from Thorn Valley recognize Ulyana's storms and beg him to stay and protect them. For one night he is wanted, needed, home. Then hunters track him there and the camp burns. Beat: belonging offered and weaponized.

chapters.title: Turn Seven
chapters.summary: POV Ryn. Halfway through the moons, Ryn decodes the ledger's cipher: the seller's mark matches Elder Maren's seal. She argues it must be forged—or that Maren traded Ulyana's soul to save the whole valley during the famine year. Beat: the group fractures over what truth is worth.

chapters.title: Sef's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Desperate to fix his old sin, Sef secretly contacts a court intermediary offering himself in Ulyana's place. The intermediary laughs: the contract is specific, the soul named. But Sef learns the payment clause—Maren's favor—is still active. Beat: sacrifice meets bureaucracy.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. The final approach to Mount Vhalen runs through a pass where the court's hunters wait in force. Ryn's plan works until it doesn't; Ulyana unleashes a full storm, and the mountain notices him. Beat: raw power, real cost—Ryn takes a wound meant for him.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Guided by Ryn's maps, they enter the under-court: a cathedral of bone and lamplight where sold souls are kept as singing glass. Ulyana hears his own voice among them. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Lady Vessarine
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Vessarine receives them courteously and shows Ulyana the truth: his parents sold half his soul to buy the valley's wards—the sanctuary itself is powered by what was taken from him. Beat: the devastating reframe; his prison was purchased with his own self.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ryn. Vessarine offers Ulyana his soul freely—if he serves the court as its storm-warden for a hundred years, keeping the valley safe forever. Belonging, purpose, protection: everything he wanted, priced in eternity. Beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. On the penultimate night, Ulyana nearly accepts. Then he touches the singing glass and hears the other sold souls—including exiles' kin—begging through it. He realizes accepting would make him complicit forever. Beat: refusal born of empathy, not heroics.

chapters.title: Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: POV Ryn. Ryn leads the actual theft while Ulyana draws the court's attention with a storm above the mountain. She swaps his soul-glass with a forgery, but Sef stays behind to hold the archive door—and is taken. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: What the Valley Is Made Of
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Fleeing, Ulyana understands the final truth: returning his soul-half will collapse the wards and expose every exile in Thorn Valley. The prophecy's last line becomes clear—it never promised he'd survive choosing. Beat: the impossible arithmetic of home.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. At the wardline under the full moon, Ulyana shatters his soul-glass rather than let either side own it. His magic floods back whole; the wards fall—but the valley's exiles, suddenly free of a sanctuary built on theft, stand together for the first time. Beat: climax—truth chosen over belonging, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: After the Storm
chapters.summary: POV Ryn. The court, cheated of its contract, withdraws; Vessarine's ledger burns when the glass breaks. Sef returns changed but alive, ransomed by the chaos. The valley rebuilds without walls. Beat: grief and relief braided together.

chapters.title: A Map Without Borders
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Months later, Ulyana—whole, unclaimed, no longer exiled so much as unhoused—sets out with Ryn and Sef to map the lands he was never allowed to see. He carries no charm, no prophecy, only weather he chose. Beat: belonging redefined as the people you walk with.
